ei.title: BRINGING NEW LIFE TO OLD CITIES
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: As cities age, neighborhoods can become old and lifeless, which may cause citizens to move away. When this happens, a collaboration between the local government and citizens is an effective way to revitalize the area. Let’s take a look at two projects in the Netherlands to find out what successful urban revitalization looks like. Wallisblok: The One-Euro Apartment Project Rotterdam, the second largest city in the Netherlands, is known for its modern architecture and busy port. By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment. Instead of crowded streets, you will see neighbors chatting in front of a modern residential structure and families spending time in its garden. The structure is a large apartment building called Wallisblok. Not that long ago, this area was very different, and nobody thought it could become a place where families would want to live. Yet that is exactly what happened. For years, the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates. Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who lived in them illegally. At first, the local government thought that the best solution was simply to tear the building down and build a new one in its place. However, having a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan. The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each. The only condition was that people who bought these apartments needed to renovate them. Although the new residents would have to pay for these renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants. Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive. They were also excited by the opportunity to use their creativity to improve the building. In the end, 42 new families moved into Wallisblok. The government’s bold plan was a success. The residents transformed the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace. The surrounding area soon began to improve as well. Today, Wallisblok is one of the most desirable places to live in Rotterdam. De Ceuvel: A Green-Technology Playground In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was full of shipyards and factories. Over time, the shipyards closed down, and the work once done at the factories was moved abroad. As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years. Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel. However, city officials did not know what to do with it. So they turned to the public for help by asking for plans that would achieve two primary goals. First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development. Second, it had to suggest a way to transform the site into a creative workspace. In the end, an architectural company submitted an innovative plan and was awarded a ten-year lease on the former shipyard. The plan was to turn the site into a sustainable office park. Since it was impossible to build foundations on the oily mud of the polluted land, the architects decided to use old, abandoned boats instead. They were able to purchase these at low prices from the boats’ owners. The architects created a small community that includes creative workspaces, studios, meeting rooms, cultural spaces, and even a café, all by upcycling the boats. Then, to connect the boats, wooden paths were built. In addition, special plants that purify polluted soil were planted across the site. Today, some people come to De Ceuvel to test new sustainable technologies such as bio-filters and water reuse systems. Many others come to experience this successful revitalization project in person. De Ceuvel is now known as one of the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology in all of Amsterdam. At the end of the lease, the project will also leave behind a more valuable piece of land for the next people who use it. These two examples of urban revitalization in the Netherlands required much more than a budget and a plan. Innovative thinking, creativity, community spirit, and cooperation were all vital to their success. These projects are great sources of inspiration for other cities that are looking to bring new life to abandoned areas.

questions.passage: As cities age, neighborhoods can become old and lifeless, which may ①<u>cause citizens to move away</u>.  When this happens, a collaboration between the local government and citizens is ②<u>an effective way to revitalize the area</u>.  Let’s take a look at two projects in the Netherlands to find out what successful urban revitalization looks like.  Wallisblok: The One-Euro Apartment Project Rotterdam, the second largest city in the Netherlands, ③<u>is known for its modern architecture</u> and busy port.  By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment.  Instead of crowded streets, you will see neighbors chatting in front of a modern residential structure and families spending time in its garden.  The structure is a large apartment building called Wallisblok.  Not that long ago, this area was very different, and nobody thought it could become a place ④<u>which families would want to live</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: which → where (관계부사: 뒤 절이 완전)
det.analysis:
① cause citizens to move away: 'which may cause citizens to move away'는 '시민들이 떠나게 만들 수 있다'예요. cause + 목적어(citizens) + to부정사(to move) 구조라 to move가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② an effective way to revitalize the area: '지역을 되살리는 효과적인 방법'이에요. 앞 명사 way를 꾸미는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사라 to revitalize가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ is known for its modern architecture: '현대적 건축으로 유명하다'예요. 로테르담이 '알려지는' 대상이므로 수동태 is known for가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ which families would want to live → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'a place ___ families would want to live'는 '가족들이 살고 싶어 하는 곳'이에요. 뒤 절(families would want to live)이 완전하고 '그곳에서 살다'라는 장소 의미이므로 관계부사 where를 써야 해요. 관계대명사 which는 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 와야 하므로 틀려요. ❌ ←정답
det.tip: 뒤 절이 완전하고 장소를 뜻하면 관계부사 where: a place where ~ live.

ch: ①

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: turning → turn (to clean up과 병렬)
det.analysis:
① that was full of shipyards and factories: 'an area ~ that was full of'는 '~으로 가득한 지역'이에요. 선행사 area를 받는 주격 관계대명사 that이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② the area was left abandoned and polluted for years: '그 지역은 수년간 버려지고 오염된 채 방치되었다'예요. be left + 분사/형용사(abandoned, polluted) 수동 구조라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ turning → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'a method to clean up the land and ___ it into a sustainable development'에서 and는 앞의 to부정사 to clean up과 짝을 이뤄야 하므로 (to) turn이 맞아요. 병렬 구조이므로 turning은 쓸 수 없어요. ❌ ←정답

④ a way to transform the site into a creative workspace: '부지를 창의적 작업 공간으로 바꿀 방법'이에요. 명사 way를 꾸미는 to부정사라 to transform이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: and로 이어진 병렬은 형태 일치: to clean up ~ and (to) turn.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: was → were (복수 병렬 주어 수 일치)
det.analysis:
① known as one of the most active playgrounds: '가장 활발한 (기술) 놀이터 중 하나로 알려져 있다'예요. be known as + 최상급 표현이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② the next people who use it: '그것을 사용할 다음 사람들'이에요. 선행사 people을 받는 주격 관계대명사 who가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ required much more than a budget and a plan: '예산과 계획 그 이상을 필요로 했다'예요. 과거시제 정동사 required와 비교 표현 much more than이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ was all vital → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 주어가 'Innovative thinking, creativity, community spirit, and cooperation'으로 and로 연결된 복수 주어예요. 따라서 복수 동사 were를 써야 하는데 단수 was는 수 일치에 어긋나요. ❌ ←정답
det.tip: A, B, C, and D처럼 and로 묶인 복수 주어는 복수 동사(were).

ch: ①
②
③

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: failure → success: 과감한 계획은 '성공'이었다
det.analysis:
✅ ① excited by the opportunity: 주민들이 창의력을 발휘할 '기회에 들떠' 있었다는 문맥에 적절해요.

❌ ② failure → success: 바로 뒤에서 42가구가 입주하고 건물이 멋지게 탈바꿈했다고 하므로 정부의 과감한 계획은 '성공(success)'이어야 해요. '실패(failure)'는 정반대라 부적절해요. ← 정답

✅ ③ The residents transformed: 주민들이 낡은 건물을 독특한 아파트로 '탈바꿈시켰다'는 과거 사실이라 적절해요.

✅ ④ began to improve as well: 주변 지역도 '나아지기 시작했다'는 긍정적 흐름에 적절해요.
det.tip: success(성공) ↔ failure(실패). 뒤 문장의 긍정적 결과로 판단하세요.

questions.passage: For years, the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates.  Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who ①<u>lived in them illegally</u>.  At first, the local government thought that the best solution was simply ②<u>to tear the building down</u> and build a new one in its place. Although the new residents would have to pay for these renovations, the government’s plan soon ④<u>attracted many applicants</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: demolish → renovate: 산 사람이 '수리해야' 한다는 조건
det.analysis:
✅ ① lived in them illegally: 버려진 아파트를 사람들이 '불법으로' 점거했다는 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ② to tear the building down: 정부가 처음엔 건물을 '허무는' 것을 최선책으로 여겼다는 문맥에 적절해요.

❌ ③ demolish → renovate: 아파트를 산 사람들이 지켜야 할 유일한 조건이에요. 바로 뒤에서 '수리 비용을 낸다(pay for these renovations)'가 이어지므로 '수리하다(renovate)'가 되어야 해요. '허물다(demolish)'는 정반대라 부적절해요. ← 정답

✅ ④ attracted many applicants: 정부의 계획이 많은 신청자를 '끌어모았다'는 문맥에 적절해요.
det.tip: renovate(수리하다) ↔ demolish(허물다). 뒤의 'pay for these renovations'가 단서.

questions.passage: Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel.  However, city officials did not know what to do with it. First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development.  Second, it had to suggest a way to __________.  In the end, an architectural company submitted an innovative plan and was awarded a ten-year lease on the former shipyard.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 = transform the site into a creative workspace(부지를 창의적 작업 공간으로 바꾸다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① transform the site into a creative workspace(부지를 창의적 작업 공간으로 바꾸다): 앞의 첫 번째(First) 목표는 '땅을 정화해 지속 가능한 개발지로 만드는 것'이고, 빈칸은 두 번째(Second) 목표예요. 이후 실제로 작업 공간·스튜디오 등이 들어선 것으로 보아 '창의적 작업 공간으로 바꾸는 것'이 자연스러워요. ← 정답

❌ ② sell the shipyard to private investors(조선소를 민간 투자자에게 팔다): 시가 직접 되살리려는 흐름과 맞지 않아요.

❌ ③ rebuild the original factory buildings(원래의 공장 건물을 다시 짓다): 공장은 이미 문을 닫았고 창의적 공간을 지향하므로 부적절해요.

❌ ④ limit public access to the area(그 지역의 대중 출입을 제한하다): 창의적 공간 조성이라는 목표와 반대예요.
det.tip: 두 목표 중 First(정화·개발) 다음의 Second → 창의적 작업 공간으로 변모.

ch: transform the site into a creative workspace
sell the shipyard to private investors
rebuild the original factory buildings
limit public access to the area

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 = much more than a budget and a plan(예산과 계획 그 이상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① only a generous government budget(넉넉한 정부 예산만): 뒤에서 '혁신적 사고·창의성·협력'이 핵심이라 했으므로 예산만으로 충분하다는 것은 반대예요.

✅ ② much more than a budget and a plan(예산과 계획 그 이상): 빈칸 뒤 문장에서 '혁신적 사고, 창의성, 공동체 정신, 협력이 모두 성공에 필수적이었다'고 하므로, 두 사례는 예산과 계획 '이상의 것'을 필요로 했다는 흐름이 자연스러워요. ← 정답

❌ ③ strict laws and heavy penalties(엄격한 법과 무거운 벌금): 본문에 법·벌금 이야기는 없어요.

❌ ④ advanced technology from abroad(해외의 첨단 기술): 글은 지역 공동체의 협력을 강조하므로 부적절해요.
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 '혁신·창의·공동체·협력이 필수'라는 말이 '예산·계획 그 이상'을 가리켜요.

ch: only a generous government budget
much more than a budget and a plan
strict laws and heavy penalties
advanced technology from abroad

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 그 동네는 '높은' 범죄율로 유명했다(낮은 범죄율 아님).
det.analysis:
① 본문 'Rotterdam, the second largest city in the Netherlands, is known for its modern architecture and busy port.'와 일치해요.

② 본문 'By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center ~ you can get to a more peaceful environment.'와 일치해요.

③ 본문은 'the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates(높은 범죄율로 유명했다)'라고 했어요. '낮은 범죄율로 안전한 지역'은 정반대이므로 불일치. ← 정답

④ 본문 'Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who lived in them illegally.'와 일치해요.
det.tip: high crime rates(높은 범죄율)를 '낮은 범죄율'로 바꾼 선지를 찾으세요.

ch: 로테르담은 네덜란드에서 두 번째로 큰 도시이며 현대적 건축과 분주한 항구로 유명하다.
도심에서 서쪽으로 트램을 10분쯤 타면 더 평화로운 환경에 닿을 수 있다.
한때 Wallisblok 일대는 낮은 범죄율로 안전한 지역으로 이름나 있었다.
Wallisblok의 많은 아파트는 버려진 뒤 불법 거주자들이 점유했다.

det.korean: 새 주민들은 수리 비용을 '직접 내야' 했다.
det.analysis:
① 본문 'the local government thought that the best solution was simply to tear the building down and build a new one in its place.'와 일치해요.

② 본문 'having a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan.'와 일치해요.

det.tip: would have to pay(직접 내야 했다)를 '전액 지원'으로 뒤집은 선지가 오답.

questions.passage: As cities age, neighborhoods can become old and lifeless, which may cause citizens to move away.  When this happens, a collaboration between the local government and citizens is an effective way to revitalize the area.  Let’s take a look at two projects in the Netherlands to find out what successful urban revitalization looks like.  Wallisblok: The One-Euro Apartment Project Rotterdam, the second largest city in the Netherlands, is known for its modern architecture and busy port.  By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment.  Instead of crowded streets, you will see neighbors chatting in front of a modern residential structure and families spending time in its garden.  The structure is a large apartment building called Wallisblok.  Not that long ago, this area was very different, and nobody thought it could become a place where families would want to live.  Yet that is exactly what happened.  For years, the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates.  Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who lived in them illegally.  At first, the local government thought that the best solution was simply to tear the building down and build a new one in its place.  However, having a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan.  The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each.  The only condition was that people who bought these apartments needed to renovate them.  Although the new residents would have to pay for these renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants.  Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive.  They were also excited by the opportunity to use their creativity to improve the building.  In the end, 42 new families moved into Wallisblok.  The government’s bold plan was a success.  The residents transformed the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace.  The surrounding area soon began to improve as well.  Today, Wallisblok is one of the most desirable places to live in Rotterdam.  De Ceuvel: A Green-Technology Playground In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was full of shipyards and factories.  Over time, the shipyards closed down, and the work once done at the factories was moved abroad.  As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years.  Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel.  However, city officials did not know what to do with it.  So they turned to the public for help by asking for plans that would achieve two primary goals.  First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development.  Second, it had to suggest a way to transform the site into a creative workspace.  In the end, an architectural company submitted an innovative plan and was awarded a ten-year lease on the former shipyard.  The plan was to turn the site into a sustainable office park.  Since it was impossible to build foundations on the oily mud of the polluted land, the architects decided to use old, abandoned boats instead.  They were able to purchase these at low prices from the boats’ owners.  The architects created a small community that includes creative workspaces, studios, meeting rooms, cultural spaces, and even a café, all by upcycling the boats.  Then, to connect the boats, wooden paths were built.  In addition, special plants that purify polluted soil were planted across the site.  Today, some people come to De Ceuvel to test new sustainable technologies such as bio-filters and water reuse systems.  Many others come to experience this successful revitalization project in person.  De Ceuvel is now known as one of the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology in all of Amsterdam.  At the end of the lease, the project will also leave behind a more valuable piece of land for the next people who use it.  These two examples of urban revitalization in the Netherlands required much more than a budget and a plan.  Innovative thinking, creativity, community spirit, and cooperation were all vital to their success.

det.analysis:
① 글은 네덜란드의 두 사례(Wallisblok의 1유로 아파트, De Ceuvel의 녹색기술 공간)를 통해 정부와 시민·대중의 협력과 창의적 발상으로 버려진 지역을 되살린 도시 재생을 다루므로 주제로 적절해요. ← 정답

det.tip: 두 사례를 관통하는 공통점 = 협력·창의를 통한 도시 재생.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology</u>가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: playground = (기술을) 활발히 시험·선보이는 '중심지' 비유.
det.analysis:
밑줄 'the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology'는 직역하면 '혁신적 녹색 기술을 위한 가장 활발한 놀이터'지만, 실제 아이들 놀이터가 아니라 새 기술을 활발히 시험하고 선보이는 '중심지'를 비유해요.

① 혁신적 녹색 기술을 활발하게 실험하고 선보이는 중심지: 바이오 필터·물 재사용 같은 신기술을 시험하러 온다는 문맥과 정확히 맞아요. ← 정답

② 아이들이 뛰어노는 놀이터를 실제로 새로 조성한 공간: playground를 글자 그대로 오해한 함정이에요.

③ 폐선을 모아 전시하는 대형 해양 박물관: 배를 재활용했을 뿐 박물관은 아니에요.

④ 정부가 직접 운영하는 대규모 친환경 발전소: 발전소라는 근거는 본문에 없어요.
det.tip: playground가 '놀이터'가 아니라 '활발한 시험·활동의 장'을 뜻하는 비유예요.

(2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: be동사 보어로 쓰인 to부정사(was to sell) 구조.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- The plan(주어): 그 계획은
- was(be동사): ~이었다
- to sell the empty apartments(보어 역할의 to부정사구): 빈 아파트들을 파는 것
- for one euro each(전치사구): 각각 1유로에
be동사 was 뒤에 to부정사가 주격보어로 와서 '그 계획은 ~하는 것이었다'가 됩니다. for ~ each는 '각각 ~에'라는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: was + to부정사(보어): '~하는 것이었다'. for one euro each = 각각 1유로에.

questions.wa: The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each
accept: The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each

questions.passage: As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years.  Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel. First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development.
questions.stem:

[단어] city / did / do / it / know / not / officials / to / what / with

det.korean: 의문사 + to부정사(what to do) 구조.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- city officials(주어): 시 공무원들
- did not know(동사): 몰랐다
- what to do with it(목적어): 그것을 어떻게 해야 할지
'what to do with ~'는 '의문사 + to부정사' 구조로 '~을 어떻게 해야 할지'라는 명사구를 만들어 know의 목적어가 됩니다.
det.tip: what to do with it = 그것을 어떻게 해야 할지(의문사 + to부정사).

questions.wa: city officials did not know what to do with it
accept: city officials did not know what to do with it

De Ceuvel: A Green-Technology Playground In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was full of shipyards and factories.  Over time, the shipyards closed down, and __________.  As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years.  Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel.  However, city officials did not know what to do with it.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'공장에서 한때 이루어지던 일은 해외로 옮겨졌다.'

[조건]
(1) abroad, at, done, factories, moved, once, the, the, was, work 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 과거분사 수식(work once done) + 수동태(was moved) 구조.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- the work(주어): 그 일은
- once done at the factories(과거분사구, work 수식): 공장에서 한때 이루어지던
- was moved abroad(수동태): 해외로 옮겨졌다
명사 work 뒤에 과거분사 done이 와서 '한때 이루어지던 일'을 꾸미고, 그 일이 '옮겨진' 대상이므로 수동태 was moved를 씁니다.
det.tip: work (which was) once done ~ : 과거분사 수식 + was moved(수동태).

questions.wa: the work once done at the factories was moved abroad
accept: the work once done at the factories was moved abroad
